title: Multiplying Whole Numbers by 10 Using Place Value

audience.delivery: voice-led visual lesson with prediction and practice

included: place value in hundreds, tens, and ones
zero as a placeholder for an empty ones place
excluded: memorised append-zero procedure as the teaching rule

learningObjective: Given a two-digit whole number, the learner will multiply it by 10 and explain that each digit moves one place left in the place-value chart, with zero recording the empty ones place.
successCriteria: Explain that 2 tens multiplied by 10 become 2 hundreds and 3 ones multiplied by 10 become 3 tens.
Place 2, 3, and 0 correctly in Hundreds, Tens, and Ones to form 230.
prerequisites: Read and write whole numbers to at least 999.
Identify hundreds, tens, and ones places.
Interpret a ten-rod as 10 ones and a hundred-flat as 10 tens.
Understand multiplication as making a quantity a stated number of times as large.

representations.concrete: unit cubes, ten-rods, and hundred-flats with visible subdivisions
representations.pictorial: persistent Hundreds–Tens–Ones chart and source-to-destination arrows

prompts: What belongs in the empty ones place?
guidedExample.supportPolicy: Show one destination arrow for the first prompt, then remove arrows and retain only column labels.

misconceptions.claim: Multiplying by 10 means just adding a zero.
misconceptions.diagnosis: Ask the learner to explain what the zero does after the non-zero digits have moved.
misconceptions.repair: Move each original digit one place left first, hold the ones place empty, then insert zero as the record of zero ones.

misconceptions.claim: The new zero pushes the other digits left.
misconceptions.diagnosis: Ask which event occurs first in the model.
misconceptions.repair: Animate the value exchange and digit shift before zero appears.

misconceptions.diagnosis: Ask where the 3 ones should move when their value becomes ten times as great.
misconceptions.repair: Show each of the 3 ones becoming a ten and occupying the Tens column.

misconceptions.diagnosis: Ask how many place-value steps correspond to one factor of 10.
misconceptions.repair: Trace exactly one column pitch from Ones to Tens and Tens to Hundreds.

chapters.purpose: Activate the problem with visible quantities and an unanswered equation.
State the child-readable objective and success criterion.
Construct 23 concretely as 2 tens and 3 ones.
Elicit direction prediction before revealing the rule.
Model the concrete, pictorial, and symbolic proof of 23 × 10.
Apply the model with fading prompts.
Measure independent transfer on an unseen number.
Retrieve the rule, zero's role, and three examples.

prediction.prompt: When multiplying 23 by 10, do the digits stay put, move one place left, or move one place right?

assessment.independent: 47 × 10 = 470 with no answer or destination arrows before commitment

feedback.203: This leaves 3 in Ones. Three ones multiplied by 10 become three tens, so 3 belongs in Tens.
feedback.2300: This moves each digit two places, which represents multiplication by 100. Multiplication by 10 moves one place.

assessment.laterRetrievalRecommendation: Recheck 47 × 10 and a structurally similar item such as 62 × 10 after at least one day.

accessibility.captionPolicy: Sentence case, synchronized to narration, never covering manipulatives or place labels.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Every color-coded state also has a label, shape, or position cue.
accessibility.reducedMotion: Replace morphs and camera moves with direct state cuts while retaining counts, origins, destinations, and pauses.
accessibility.thinkingWindows: No narration and no answer reveal during specified silence.
